verdict.rationale: Deepgram documents its own temporary tokens with a 30-second TTL that give time-limited access to its APIs as an alternative to long-lived API keys, which partially limits credential privilege for real-time agent clients. The evidence shows only time-bounding, not permission scoping or a least-privilege role model. missing for 10: documented scope/permission restrictions on keys or tokens, per-agent credential issuance, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: A temporary token is a secure, authentication credential that provides time-limited access to Deepgram's APIs. These tokens have a 30 second Time To Live (TTL)
Unlike traditional API keys, temporary tokens are ideal for real-time applications requiring secure, temporary access to Deepgram's services.
